Verification Principles

How we evaluate product claims.

The framework below separates evidence requirements from records that have actually been supplied.

01

Audited Scope & Issuer

A legitimate certification should name the manufacturing facility, legal entity, issuing body, and exact product category covered.

02

Active Document Validity

Testing reports and compliance licenses possess strict expiration dates. We mandate recurrent audit cycles rather than relying on legacy or unmaintained approvals.

03

Claim Alignment

Traditional herbal context should be distinguished from laboratory validation, and specifications published only when supporting evidence is available.

Laboratory Integrity

What customers should look for.

When inspecting herbal products, discerning consumers prioritize verifiable proof over promotional rhetoric:

  • Certificate of Analysis: Match the batch number, issue date, laboratory, and tested specification.
  • Contaminant screening: Check which metals, microbes, or residues were tested and the limits applied.
  • Identity records: Confirm botanical name, plant part, origin, and the method used to identify it.

Does “not supplied” mean a standard has failed?

No. It means this public template does not contain client evidence that supports a verified status.

What should a product-specific document request include?

Include the product name and batch or lot number, if available, so the request can be matched to the correct record.
